pageCache.pageTitle: Head’s Welcome | Francis Holland Regent’s Park
pageCache.text:
HEAD’S WELCOME
Founded in 1878, Francis Holland Regent’s Park has a long-standing history of combining educational excellence with empathy. This is a happy school and I never cease to be amazed by what our girls achieve.
As a leading day school, academic standards are high with an excellent culture of pastoral care woven into our fabric. Set in the heart of London, with all the opportunities and energy that brings, we are a community like no other. Our four values – Compassion, Knowledge, Perseverance and Spirit – underpin everything, creating a strong sense of purpose and belonging.
Francis Holland Regent’s Park is forward-thinking in an ever-changing world. Our educational offer is centred on the futures of our girls. We also want to empower them to be bold, ambitious and free from the shackles of perfectionism. Nothing should hold them back; they can be themselves, develop their strengths and discover their passions.
Our pupils leave us as grounded young women with a strong moral compass, knowing what they want and who they want to be.
Mrs Katharine Woodcock Head

pageCache.pageTitle: Ethos & Values | Francis Holland Regent’s Park
pageCache.text:
ETHOS & VALUES
We are a values-led school committed to nurturing academically ambitious, compassionate and confident young people. Through a rich, inclusive and personalised education, we inspire curiosity, develop character and empower every girl to thrive, contribute positively to their community, and shape a better future.
OUR VALUES
Our pupils are guided to respect and celebrate others’ differences and needs. They’re encouraged to be kind, considerate and support our pupil-led charitable initiative: the Help Fund. They should be able to demonstrate empathy in everyday life and make a positive contribution to society.
Curious, intellectually enquiring, ambitious, forward thinking, creative, imaginative, seeking challenge and inspiration – that’s how we think of our pupils. We hope they’ll foster a lifelong love of learning and embrace the many academic and co-curricular opportunities available here.
We encourage pupils to be bold, resilient and flexible so they can adapt to the demands of an ever-changing world. They’re free to take risks, step out of their comfort zone and develop strength and inner confidence to overcome challenge and adversity. We celebrate effort as well as achievement and contribution.
We’re a Church of England school with Christian values and are respectful and mindful of different faiths and beliefs. Our pupils are proud of our FHS spirit: our history, traditions and community.
Where next?

CLOSE-KNIT
Francis Holland Regent’s Park is, above all, a close-knit community. Our Senior School at Ivor Place and Sixth Form at Linhope House blend tradition with modernity, creating a welcoming environment where girls feel at home and inspired to become their best selves.
INSPIRE FUTURE
As we approach our 150th year, we remain true to the supportive spirit that has defined us since 1878. Pupils, staff, parents, alumni and Governors all contribute their unique qualities to our shared story.
With every passing day, our community grows more vibrant, distinctive, and united, carrying forward the legacy of countless women who have walked our halls and become leaders, innovators, and advocates.
At the heart of Francis Holland Regent’s Park is a sisterhood that uplifts, empowers, and celebrates every achievement. Our founder, Canon Francis Holland, envisioned a place where girls could grow in wisdom and grace – a vision that continues to thrive today.
LIFELONG BONDS
Alumni – Quondam, the Francis Holland Regent’s Park Old Girls’ Association, is a vibrant and supportive community open to all former pupils and staff (hence our use of alumni, not alumnae!). It plays a vital role in maintaining the lifelong friendships and professional connections that begin during school and continue well beyond.
At the heart of this community is our dedicated alumni network website, where members can register their details, reconnect with old friends, and build an exclusive professional network. The platform features news updates, photo galleries, upcoming events, and a career mentoring hub that brings together generations of FHRP alumni.
Discover our Community
Where next?

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome to Francis Holland Regent’s Park - Independent Day School for Girls
pageCache.text:
WELCOME
We know choosing a school is a really big decision and our Admissions team is on hand to provide all the answers you need to help you on this journey and ultimately ensure you and your daughter make the best choice. Visit our dedicated pages below for all the information you'll need.
"If you want a school where your daughter will be nurtured and encouraged to develop as a well-rounded person in a supportive (not 'hot-house') environment, with the opportunity to excel academically, Francis Holland Regent's Park would be an excellent choice."
- PARENT OF CLASS OF 2026 LEAVER
VISIT US
Experience first-hand the vibrant life of our School – where curiosity is celebrated, confidence takes root, and futures begin to take shape.
You’ll meet our passionate teachers, hear directly from our bright, articulate girls, and enjoy an insightful address from our Head.
FEES
All fees are inclusive of VAT unless otherwise stated.
Registration Fees (effective 1 July 2026) UK Residents – £200 Overseas Residents – £265
Termly School Fees (effective 1 September 2026)* Year 7 to Year 13 – £10,845
Fees are subject to an annual review
Termly school fees are inclusive of lunches and Personal Accident Insurance.
BURSARIES & SCHOLARSHIPS
Francis Holland Regent’s Park is committed to providing a service to the local and wider community.
One of the Francis Holland Schools Trust’s key objectives is to offer a first class education to children who would not otherwise be able to afford it. Our provision of bursary awards has always been a priority to the Trust and over the years we are delighted that so many girls have been able to benefit from an FHRP education, despite their financial circumstances.
“Francis Holland Regent's Park has been everything we had hoped for. Our girls are thriving, they have made lots of new friends and there is not a day that they don’t come home brimming with enthusiasm about everything that’s been going on that day”
Where next?

pageCache.pageTitle: Senior School at Francis Holland Regent’s Park - Independent Girls Day School
pageCache.text:
PROUDLY PURPOSEFUL.
Welcome to a school that’s decisively, distinctively and definitively London. A school where you can belong and be you.
THE BEST OF BOTH WORLDS
Francis Holland Regent’s Park is an academically selective school in the heart of London for girls aged 11–18. We’re a diverse and dynamic community that draws pupils from a wide range of preparatory and primary schools.
Being on the edge of Regent’s Park brings so many advantages: the culture, pace and buzz of London with the greenery and space of the park.
Four forms in each year group and small class sizes at GCSE mean everyone receives personalised attention and expert and adaptive teaching, so that they can unlock what’s already inside. Academic results matter, but so does having the confidence, curiosity and skills to thrive in life.
STEM, music, drama, art, and sport are strong here. Our on-site swimming pool, six science labs, dedicated art studios, recently transformed library and the Gloucester Wing with its seminar rooms and flexible teaching spaces set us apart. Purpose-built spaces, such as the Helen McCrory Drama Studio and Linhope House, our Sixth Form Centre, support creative learning and academic ambition.
Welcome to the best of everything.
"Recent results have been stellar, propelling it sharply up league tables. At GCSE, they average one grade higher than baseline predictions, placing school in top 30 independent schools in the country in terms of value added."
Discover Senior School
LEADERSHIP
We offer lots of ways in which pupils can shape their tomorrows at school and beyond.
There are opportunities to lead by being a Form Captain, or a Society President later on. There are chances to organise events, lead assemblies, represent peers and support the wider school community. Being part of a team in a club, society or sport are other brilliant ways to show initiative and learn resilience.
Where next?

We’re here for your future, your way. Develop new skills. Embrace new challenges. It’s all yours for the taking.
Sixth Form here isn’t just about A Levels… our enrichment programme and leadership opportunities will help prepare you for higher education and the world of work. Strong pastoral care, smaller teaching groups and a friendly community are what define us.

That’s not all. You’ve got the greenery and space of Regent’s Park a short walk away, and the culture, pace and buzz of London life at your fingertips.

Our Sixth Form Centre, Linhope House, offers a modern, spacious environment that blends elegant Georgian features with state-of-the-art facilities. With study spaces, a Think Lab, and natural light-filled areas, it provides the perfect setting for academic and personal growth, bridging the gap between school and university life.
Designed with input from Sixth Form students, the interior boasts a calm, Scandinavian-style decor, featuring natural materials and a bio-farm plant wall to promote wellbeing. Just a two-minute walk from our main site, Linhope House gives our students independence while keeping them connected with the wider school community.

pageCache.pageTitle: Partnerships & Outreach | Francis Holland Regent’s Park
pageCache.text:
PARTNERSHIPS & OUTREACH
We are proud to work in close partnership with local state schools through a wide range of initiatives. Each year, every department in our school is encouraged to run a dedicated partnership programme, reflecting our commitment to sharing expertise and resources with the wider community.
PERFECT SYNERGY.
These collaborations include sharing teaching staff and facilities, organising joint projects, hosting mock Oxbridge interviews, coordinating volunteering schemes, and fundraising for our charity partners. Staff and pupils alike work hard to ensure our partnerships are meaningful, impactful, and far-reaching.
One of our longest-standing partnerships is with St Marylebone CE School. In addition to providing Physics tuition and Oxbridge mentoring, our teachers offer Latin lessons to girls in Years 8–11. We also host an annual Classics Symposium, welcoming over 100 students from across London and the South East for a day of interactive lectures delivered by leading Oxbridge academics.
Our Modern Foreign Languages department runs subject-specific study days, including our annual German Day, attended by more than 150 pupils from partner schools in London and Bristol. We also host an annual Physics Symposium for students from local schools.
SHARED VISION.
In collaboration with St Marylebone CE School, we participate in the RIBA Architectural Programme, offering a series of workshops led by prominent industry professionals.
Our Lower Sixth Sports Leaders regularly visit a local primary school to coach gymnastics to Year 3 pupils. During the Easter holidays, the Economics department organises an A Level study day, inviting students from schools across the country to take part.
We also enjoy longstanding relationships with Swiss Cottage School and St Vincent’s Catholic Primary School at which a number of Lower Sixth students volunteer regularly. Pupils from St Vincent’s attend our theatre productions, and we work together on STEM initiatives, such as our student-led Rockets and Robots workshop, hosted on their site.
Together, these initiatives reflect our deep-rooted commitment to educational partnership, community engagement, and widening access for all.
Where next?

pageCache.text:
ACADEMIC RESULTS & DESTINATIONS
At Francis Holland Regent's Park, academic achievement has long been a hallmark of our school.
We foster a learning environment that is both nurturing and intellectually demanding, where passionate subject experts inspire students to explore ideas beyond the syllabus. Every year, our A Level students secure places on prestigious and competitive degree courses at leading universities in the UK and around the world.
Our academic outcomes are consistently outstanding. Our girls excel across a broad range of subjects, earning top marks in national and international examinations.
GCSE RESULTS
We would like to congratulate our wonderful Upper Fifth on their outstanding GCSE results.
These results reflect their hard work, resilience and determination, as well as the expertise and unwavering support of their teachers. We are immensely proud of all they have achieved and look forward to welcoming them to Linhope House for Sixth Form in September.
“Congratulations to our Upper Fifth on their excellent GCSE results. These results are a reflection of their genuine effort, determination and character, and they should be enormously proud of what they have achieved. We are delighted for each and every one of them and hugely excited to welcome them to Linhope House as they embark on the next exciting chapter of their school journey.”
–KATHARINE WOODCOCK, HEAD
5 GCSEs grade 9 - 4 / A* - C
GCSE Results
A LEVEL RESULTS
We could not be prouder of the achievements of our Sixth Formers.
We are thrilled to celebrate another stellar set of results, with an impressive 92% of A Level grades awarded at A–B*. Our Class of 2026 are heading to leading UK universities including Bristol, Durham, Edinburgh, Imperial College London and UCL, as well as prestigious overseas institutions including Rice University, McGill, Bocconi and IE Madrid.
Our leavers will pursue an exciting and diverse range of courses, reflecting their individual talents, passions and ambitions, and the breadth of opportunities available at Francis Holland Regent’s Park.
They leave us equipped not only with exceptional qualifications, but also with the confidence, compassion, curiosity and breadth of experience that come from embracing the many opportunities school life has to offer. We are confident they will continue to thrive, making a positive impact and shaping a bright future wherever their journeys take them.
A Level Results
EPQ RESULTS
The Extended Project Qualification is a national course, which is considered the equivalent of half an A Level course.
The EPQ rewards independent research, thought and curiosity. Students choose to complete either a 5000-word research project or an artefact with a supporting 1000-word report. At the end of the project, students present their findings to an audience, showcasing a range of innovative and impressive topic areas. The course is enormously beneficial, developing transferable skills to equip students for learning at university. The course is highly-regarded by universities and the pass rates at Francis Holland Regent’s Park are far above national norms.
EPQ Results
DESTINATIONS
At Francis Holland Regent’s Park, our pupils consistently secure places at some of the world’s leading universities.
Recent leavers have gone on to study at renowned institutions including Oxford and Cambridge, Imperial College, UCL, Durham University and leading overseas universities across Europe and North America.
Our students pursue a diverse range of subjects – from Medicine, Veterinary Medicine, Law, and Engineering to Humanities, the Arts, and Social Sciences – reflecting the breadth and depth of academic excellence fostered at FHRP. This strong track record demonstrates our commitment to supporting and preparing young women not only for academic success but for leadership and impact in their chosen fields.
Parents can be confident that a Francis Holland Regent’s Park education equips pupils with the knowledge, skills, and ambition not only to gain entry to top-tier universities worldwide but thrive once there.
“My time at FHRP has been foundational in shaping both my academic and personal development. I am truly grateful for the encouragement, guidance, and inspiration I received throughout my years at the school.”
—Class of 2025 Leaver
Where next?

pageCache.pageTitle: Governors & Staff | Francis Holland Regent’s Park
pageCache.text:
GOVERNORS & STAFF
The three schools are led by a Board of Governors, known as The Council, made up of 13 members who bring a wealth of experience and expertise to the non-executive leadership of the schools.
MRS KATHARINE WOODCOCK
Head of Francis Holland Regent’s Park
Mrs Woodcock joined Francis Holland Regent’s Park as Head in September 2022. She was previously Head of Sydenham High School GDST, and prior to this held a number of senior leadership positions elsewhere, including Head of Sixth Form and Senior Deputy Head.
Mrs Woodcock read French and Russian at Bristol University and taught abroad before completing her PGCE at St Mary’s, Twickenham. Mrs Woodcock comes from a long line of teachers, and her first teaching post was as a languages teacher and resident tutor at Oakham School, Rutland, where she later became a Housemistress.
Mrs Woodcock is a governor in two schools, including Hurstpierpoint College. She is a member of the HMC Professional Development Committee, sits on the Independent Schools Teacher Induction Panel (ISTip) and is Co-Chair of the 11+ Consortium. Mrs Woodcock is married with two grown up children and in her spare time enjoys running, travel and spending time with her family.
Our Senior Leadership Team
Amelia SlocombeSenior Deputy Head
Amelia SlocombeSenior Deputy Head
Amelia began teaching in 1995 and taught French and Italian in two London day schools before re-training and working in the city as a banking regulatory lawyer for 10 years.
She returned to teaching in 2011 in the Modern Foreign Languages department at Francis Holland Regent’s Park and subsequently held the positions of Director of Higher Education and Head of Sixth Form until becoming Senior Deputy Head in 2016.
Kay HotchkissDeputy Head (Academic)
Kay HotchkissDeputy Head (Academic)
Colette Mahieu Deputy Head (Pastoral and Safeguarding)
Colette Mahieu Deputy Head (Pastoral and Safeguarding)
Colette holds a Bachelor of Education in Human Movement and Health Education from the University of Sydney and a Master’s in Sociology of Education with Distinction from University College London (UCL). Her master’s research focused on adolescence and social media, with a particular emphasis on sexual harassment and teenage girls.
As Deputy Head Pastoral, a role that Colette has been doing since 2012, she is dedicated to fostering a supportive and inclusive environment for all pupils. Her approach to pastoral care is rooted in understanding the unique challenges faced by adolescents today, and she is committed to promoting their well-being and personal growth.
Outside of her professional life, Colette continues to play competitive tennis and enjoys the lively challenge of keeping up with her two toddlers, who help her to stay fit and energised!
Sarah HackAssistant Head (Co-curricular and Operations)
Sarah HackAssistant Head (Co-curricular and Operations)
Sarah studied Geography and Economics at Portsmouth University, before undertaking her PGCE at Southampton University. Now in her 26th year of teaching, she has been at Francis Holland Regent’s Park since 2007, before which she taught at state schools in Oxfordshire, Tooting and Enfield. Having previously been Head of Geography at Francis Holland for ten years, Sarah was appointed as Assistant Head (Operations and Co-curricular) in 2017. Her role is varied, including Health and Safety, Trips and Visits, and the day-to-day logistics of the school.
She oversees the co-curricular provision which currently runs at 90 clubs a week. In her free time, Sarah enjoys the outdoors, being an avid golfer and birdwatcher.
Nick GridelliAssistant Head (Head of Sixth Form)
Nick GridelliAssistant Head (Head of Sixth Form)
With a First Class Honours degree in Modern Foreign Languages from Bologna University, a PGCE from the Institute of Education, and a Master’s in Leadership in Education from UCL/IOE, Nick brings academic rigour and deep experience to his role. He joined Francis Holland Regent’s Park in 2010 as Head of Italian, later becoming Head of Modern Foreign Languages, before moving into pastoral leadership in 2017. As Deputy Designated Safeguarding Lead (DDSL), he has extensive first-hand experience in safeguarding and student wellbeing.
Nick is passionate about girls’ education and empowerment, and a strong advocate for mental fitness, a growth mindset, and the values of diversity and equality. Known for his empathy and good sense of humour, he believes deeply in the power of human relationships and open dialogue, and considers it a privilege to support students during this crucial phase of their education and personal development.
In his free time, Nick a wellbeing and nutrition enthusiast, former volleyball player, and keen traveller who enjoys putting his language skills into practice wherever he goes.
Emily MorganAssistant Head (Teaching & Learning) (maternity cover)
Emily MorganAssistant Head (Teaching & Learning) (maternity cover)
Emily joined Francis Holland Regent’s Park in 2019 and was appointed Head of Mathematics in 2021. Prior to this, Emily has taught Mathematics in Cambridge, Bristol and for a short time abroad, at Yale University. Emily is currently Acting Assistant Head Teaching & Learning, where she oversees the Oxbridge provision and Academic Stretch & Challenge.
Emily studied Natural Sciences at Gonville & Caius College, Cambridge and then completed an MSci in the Psychology of Education at the University of Bristol. Her Masters explored growth mindset, self-efficacy and motivation in Mathematics Education. Emily is passionate about empowering females in STEM.
In her spare time, Emily loves the outdoors and is an avid ultra-marathon runner. She also enjoys bike-packing across Europe, reading and camping.
Jo DawesAssistant Head (Teaching & Learning) (maternity cover)
Jo DawesAssistant Head (Teaching & Learning) (maternity cover)
Jo has been a member of the school community since 2013 and currently serves as Assistant Head of Teaching and Learning, alongside her role as Head of Geography, a position held since 2017. Jo holds a BA in Geography and Economics from the University of Nottingham, a PGCE from the Institute of Education, and a Master’s degree in Geography in Education from UCL.
As the school’s Environmental Lead, Jo is passionate about sustainability and about instilling strong leadership qualities in pupils. Outside of school, Jo enjoys spending time with her two daughters and playing netball socially.
Eleanor Chapman Assistant Head (Teaching & Learning) (maternity leave)
Eleanor Chapman Assistant Head (Teaching & Learning) (maternity leave)
Eleanor joined Francis Holland Regent’s Park in 2020 as Head of English, following her tenure at Latymer Upper School in Hammersmith. She was appointed to her current role in January 2025, bringing with her a deep commitment to academic excellence and staff development.
Eleanor holds a BA in English Literature with a minor in Art History from Newcastle University, a PGCE from the Institute of Education, and an MA in English in Education from King’s College London. Eleanor is passionate about empowering teaching staff to continually refine their practice and has played a key role in mentoring Early Career Teachers and PGCE students through a robust induction programme.
Outside of school, Eleanor enjoys spending time with her son, reading, cycling and exploring art galleries.
Stephanie LambChief Operating Officer
Stephanie LambChief Operating Officer
Stephanie is a former Tax Partner at EY, with over 25 years of experience in the professional services sector. She is a qualified Chartered Accountant and Chartered Tax Advisor. Over the course of her 16-year tenure as Partner, Stephanie undertook a variety of senior leadership roles in parallel with her client service responsibilities, including serving as a member of EY’s Global Tax Executive, the body responsible for setting the strategic direction of the global tax practice.
Passionate about the transformative power of education to enable individuals to achieve their ambitions, Stephanie brings extensive expertise in leadership, communication, operational transformation, and delivery excellence. She is committed to applying this experience to ensure the continued sustainability and growth of the Francis Holland Schools Trust and, in so doing, supporting and enabling the next generation for success.
Matt Britland Director of Technology
Matt Britland Director of Technology
With over 20 years of experience in education, Matt has worked across both the maintained and independent sectors. His journey in independent education began in 2010 at Kingston Grammar School, followed by roles at The Lady Eleanor Holles School in 2014 and Alleyn’s School in 2018. In 2023, he joined the Francis Holland Schools Trust, continuing his commitment to excellence in teaching and learning and the implementation of technology across all parts of school life.
Matt is passionate about the transformative role of technology in education and its potential to empower all staff and students. Beyond the classroom, he has a keen interest in collecting trainers and vinyl records. Music is a significant part of Matt’s life and he enjoys mixing and producing music in his spare time, blending creativity with technical skill.
His diverse interests reflect a lifelong love of learning, innovation, and culture.
Tom RobertsonDirector of Development
Tom RobertsonDirector of Development
As Director of Development, Tom leads on fundraising and engagement strategies. Tom has over 15 years’ experience in the independent school sector, previously heading up development for the Alpha Plus Group, working with 12 independent schools and three sixth form colleges in the UK and overseas and before that at Bradfield College, Berkshire.
Passionate about widening access to independent education, since joining the Trust in 2021 Tom has launched endowment campaigns for transformational bursaries at both Francis Holland Regent’s Park and Francis Holland Sloane Square. He also serves as a Governor of Elstree School in Berkshire. Outside work, Tom enjoys walking, travelling, and playing real tennis.
Ben TaylorDirector of HR
Ben TaylorDirector of HR
Ben holds a BA in Management and Human Resources from the University of Hull and is a Chartered Member of the CIPD. He joined the Francis Holland Schools Trust in September 2023, and has 7 years’ experience in the education sector, prior to which he held roles in local government, travel leisure and tourism. Ben’s focus is to provide efficient and effective HR systems and processes to support our colleagues to achieve their very best.
Ben enjoys the theatre, dining out and travelling and was fortunate enough to be able to travel the world with work in one of his previous roles.
Where next?

pageCache.pageTitle: Upper Fifth Celebrate Outstanding GCSE Results | Francis Holland Regent’s Park
pageCache.text:
Upper Fifth Celebrate Outstanding GCSE Results
The wait is finally over for our outgoing Upper Fifth pupils, who received their GCSE results this morning following years of dedication, perseverance and hard work. Many congratulations to them all.
Today is a day of great pride for pupils, families and staff alike. The Upper Fifth’s results are a reflection not only of academic achievement, but also of the enthusiasm, resilience and determination they have shown throughout their time at Francis Holland Regent’s Park. We are thrilled to celebrate their success and immensely proud of all that they have accomplished, both within and beyond the classroom.
This year, 36% of all grades were awarded at Grade 9, 66% of grades were awarded 9-8 and 85% of grades were awarded 9-7. These excellent outcomes are testament to the commitment of our pupils and to the support, expertise and encouragement provided by their teachers.
GCSE results represent much more than a set of grades. They reflect countless hours of study, superb time management and organisation, and the ability to balance academic commitments with participation in co-curricular activities and contributions to school life. We are especially proud of the way this year group has approached challenges with maturity, kindness and determination, embodying the values that define our school community. The personal growth that takes place throughout these important years should not be underestimated.
“What a wonderful morning. Our Upper Fifth pupils should be enormously proud of what they have achieved. These results are the product of genuine effort, determination and character. We are delighted for each and every one of them and hugely excited to welcome them to our wonderful Sixth Form Centre, Linhope House, in a couple of weeks as they embark on the next exciting chapter of their school journey.
“We hope they enjoy the final weeks of the summer break and look forward to welcoming them back very soon. Many congratulations to them all.”
– Katharine Woodcock, Head
As they celebrate their achievements today, our Upper Fifth pupils can look forward with confidence to the next stage of their education. Their GCSE results provide a strong foundation for future academic and personal success and place them in an excellent position as they progress into Sixth Form.
We are excited to welcome the year group to Linhope House in September, where they will embark on new academic challenges, develop greater independence and benefit from the wealth of opportunities that our Sixth Form Centre offers. Having already demonstrated such commitment and capability, we have every confidence that they will continue to flourish and make the most of the exciting years ahead.
While today is a celebration of examination success, it is also an opportunity to recognise everything this exceptional cohort has contributed to the life of the school. We are immensely proud of the young women they have become and look forward to supporting them as they begin this next chapter.
Congratulations once again to our outstanding Upper Fifth. We wish them a wonderful summer and look forward to seeing them settle into Linhope House very soon.

pageCache.pageTitle: Founded in 1878 | Francis Holland Regent’s Park
pageCache.text:
FOUNDED IN 1878
On Tuesday 1 October 1878, a small group of girls gathered outside 6 Upper Baker Street to start their school days at what was known then as The Church of England High School for Girls, founded by the Reverend Canon Francis Holland.
SINCE 1878.
The School remained at the Baker Street site until 1915 when it was transferred to its purpose built site near Clarence Gate, where it remains today.
We remain true to our founding principles as pioneers of girls’ education, underpinned by our Christian ethos, with an unwavering commitment to education, centred on excellence, character, creativity, sustainability and community.
In October 2028, with the capacity to welcome just under 600 girls, our school will celebrate 150 years of educating girls, of guiding both hearts and minds; an enormous milestone in the history of our School. Today and tomorrow, we continue to cherish our heritage and history, blending tradition with innovation in the pursuit of excellence.
Where next?

pageCache.pageTitle: The Heart of London | Francis Holland Regent’s Park
pageCache.text:
THE HEART OF LONDON
We are a true microcosm of London, with a richly diverse pupil body drawn from both state and independent primary schools, locally and from further afield.
CITY SMART.
Our central location, just a short distance from Baker Street, makes us easily accessible. Our pupils commute from across the city, supported by excellent public transport links, including numerous bus routes and our close proximity to Baker Street station.
Space in central London is limited, but we are fortunate to have Regent’s Park right on our doorstep. Our pupils make daily use of its outstanding outdoor facilities for both sport and leisure. Lunchtime outings are supervised for pupils in the Thirds and Lower Fourth, while those in the Upper Fourth to Upper Fifth may go out in groups of three. We also use Paddington Recreation Ground for athletics and hockey, with a smooth and reliable bus service transporting pupils to and from the site.
Our location offers unrivalled access to London’s world-class cultural and academic institutions. Pupils across all year groups enjoy regular visits to cultural and academic landmarks such as the EY and BNP Paribas Headquarters, Westminster Abbey, and the Bank of England, enriching their learning with real-world experiences.
While Francis Holland Regent’s Park is rooted in Anglican tradition, we warmly welcome pupils of all faiths and none. Every year group reflects this inclusivity, with a wide range of beliefs represented across the school community.

SAFEGUARDING
At Francis Holland Regent’s Park we are committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of all our pupils.
SAFEGUARDING
All staff, whether teachers or support staff, undertake regular safeguarding training and are confident to act on and report any concerns.
For any enquiries or concerns about safeguarding, please refer to the Safeguarding Team:
Ms Colette Mahieu Deputy Head Pastoral and Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL) colette.mahieu@fhs-nw1.org.uk
Mr Nick Gridelli Assistant Head, Head of Sixth Form and Deputy Designated Safeguarding Lead (DDSL) nicola.gridelli@fhs-nw1.org.uk
Ms Maria Merrigan Head of Middle School and DDSL maria.merrigan@fhs-nw1.org.uk
Dr Nesrine El Akel Head of Lower School and DDSL nesrine.el-akel@fhs-nw1.org.uk
Ms Steph Simoni Safeguarding and Attendance Officer and Deputy Designated Safeguarding Lead steph.simoni@fhs-nw1.org.uk
The school provides counselling services for our pupils. They can be referred by a member of staff or self-refer by contacting counsellor@fhs-nw1.org.uk and this service is private and confidential.
We subscribe to the Mix Connect, a mental health support service that offer a variety of support options, including articles, online community, local organisation finder and more.
URGENT SAFEGUARDING MATTERS
For urgent safeguarding matters which fall outside school hours please contact children’s services for the borough of the child’s residence or call 999 in an emergency. Other helpful contacts:
Childline 0800 1111
The Mix 0808 808 4994
Shout crisis support (text) 85258

pageCache.pageTitle: Sixth Form Podcast Receives Commendation in National Kew Gardens Competition | Francis Holland Regent’s Park
pageCache.text:
Sixth Form Podcast Receives Commendation in National Kew Gardens Competition
Congratulations to Lower Sixth pupils and hosts of The Science Study Booth podcast, who have received a commendation in this year’s Kew Gardens Endeavour Competition Challenge.
The pair submitted a special podcast episode exploring the growing importance of green careers, highlighting both traditional and non-traditional pathways into sustainability-focused professions. Drawing on extensive research, they discussed routes into green careers, showcased a range of exciting opportunities and even included an interactive quiz for listeners.
The judging panel at Kew Gardens were highly impressed by the submission, praising the pupils’ “very natural, comfortable conversation style”, strong rapport as presenters and the depth of their research. Judges also highlighted the podcast’s clear structure, insightful discussion of green careers and creative approach to engaging listeners.
While the competition was fiercely contested, the pupils were awarded a commendation certificate in recognition of the quality of their work and the care, thought and creativity that went into the project.
We are incredibly proud of their achievement and delighted to see The Science Study Booth recognised by such a prestigious national competition. Their success is a wonderful example of the intellectual curiosity, communication skills and passion for scientific enquiry that we seek to foster at Francis Holland Regent’s Park.
Well done to both pupils on this fantastic achievement!
